findings.evidence: "Passengers can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."

findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Weekend zone status" inside the table.

findings.evidence: "Local residents should review the updated schedule through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Rewrite the second sentence to match the actual action, e.g. "Station staff can also help you find the updated schedule in person."
findings.violation: The second sentence refers to "the same request," but the first sentence describes reviewing a schedule, not making a request - this is leftover boilerplate copied from the fare-adjustment paragraphs that no longer makes sense in context.

findings.evidence: "Passengers should review the updated schedule through the mobile app. The change takes effect on the following service day."
findings.fix: Merge the effective-date sentence into s3-p1 and delete this paragraph, or replace it with distinct content.
findings.violation: Duplicates the "review the updated schedule through the mobile app" instruction already given in s3-p1 immediately above, adding only the effective-date sentence as new information.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: State the real effective date or a concrete rule for finding it, e.g. "Route adjustments take effect on the date shown on the alert for your route."
findings.violation: Tautological statement ("take effect on the effective date") that conveys no actual date or useful information.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate and write content specific to schedule changes, or consolidate real-time arrival info into a single location.
findings.violation: Near-duplicate of s1-p2 under "Accessibility improvements," pasted into an unrelated "Schedule changes" card with only "Passengers"→"Local residents" swapped.

findings.fix: Use a `<button>` element (or add `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, and keyboard handlers) with an `aria-label="Delete"` or similar.
findings.violation: A clickable-looking delete icon is implemented as a plain `<div>` with an empty-alt image, giving it no accessible name, role, or keyboard focusability.

` appears first in the markup, followed by step2 then step1 (order:1)
findings.fix: Reorder the elements in the HTML source to match the intended reading/visual sequence instead of relying on CSS `order`.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list`
findings.fix: Change the link text to accurately describe the destination, e.g. "view fare adjustment history," or point the href at the actual accessibility list if that was intended.
findings.violation: The link text ("read the accessibility improvements list") matches neither the surrounding sentence ("full list of upcoming adjustments") nor its destination URL (`/fares/history`), making the link's purpose unclear or misleading.

findings.fix: Add a visible text/symbol cue (e.g., "Phone number (required)") in addition to or instead of the color.
findings.violation: The label is styled red with no accompanying text or symbol, so any meaning conveyed by the color (e.g., required field) is lost on users who can't perceive color.

findings.fix: Remove the hardcoded `aria-invalid="true"` from the default markup, add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` on the input, and replace "Error." with a specific message (e.g., "Promo code not recognized").
findings.location: Section "Schedule changes", form promo field (input#promo and s3-form-promo-error)
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded in the static markup so the field is announced as invalid before any user input, and the error text is not programmatically linked to the input via `aria-describedby`, nor is "Error." descriptive of the actual problem.

findings.evidence: `<select id="topic">...`, `<input id="email" type="email">`, `<input id="phone" type="tel">`, `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">`
findings.fix: Add a `name` attribute to each control, e.g. `name="route"`, `name="email"`, `name="phone"`, `name="promo"`.
findings.violation: None of the form controls have a `name` attribute, so submitting the form would send no field data to the server.
